description.narrative: Gender Transformative and Responsible agribusiness Investment in South East Asia (GRAISEA) aims to demonstrate that business in the agricultural sector in South East (SE) Asia, can be a driver of human rights, women's economic empowerment and climate resilience. Working in the Philippines, Indonesia, Cambodia, Vietnam and Pakistan, GRAISEA 2 aims to be a catalyst, bringing about systemic change in how business operates through influencing at four levels: Value chains: Within the rice and shrimp sectors, GRAISEA 2 supports the development of more inclusive and responsible value chains working with producer groups and small, medium and large companies. Multi stakeholder initiatives: GRAISEA 2 collaborates with and influences sectoral multi -stakeholder initiatives (MSIs), as a means to reach more companies and to influence standards to be more supportive of women's economic empowerment and climate resilience. National policy: To create a more enabling environment for inclusive and responsible business, advocacy is supported on sector -based policy as well as on national frameworks for the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Regional policy: To support a regional enabling environment, the programme engages with a number of Association of South East Asian Nation (ASEAN) institutions and frameworks including the regional strategy for business and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and regional Micro Small and Medium -Sized Enterprise (MSME) policy. The project allows the Programme Management Unit (PMU) to ensure overall delivery of the programme and contract management towards the implementing partners. Specifically the PMU will manage relationships with - five Oxfam country programmes (Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia, Pakistan and Cambodia) - five regional implementing partners; Business and Human Rights Resource Centre, Asian Seafood Improvement Collaboration, Weaving Women's Rig
